crisis.title: The ocean has already passed its limits.
crisis.lead: Ocean pollution is no longer an issue for environmental groups alone; it is a business risk that extends to supply chains, brands, investor ratings, and regulation.

items.label: Plastic entering the ocean each year
items.desc: In the North Pacific, a giant garbage patch roughly 16 times the size of South Korea has formed.

items.label: Marine debris generated along Korea's coasts
items.desc: More than half goes uncollected, threatening ecosystems as it sinks to the seabed or drifts.

items.label: Annual losses from ghost fishing
items.desc: Fishing losses caused by abandoned ghost nets. Microplastics ultimately return to our dinner tables.

crisis.note: Since 2024, the government has been tightening regulations aimed at reducing the net generation of marine debris (Net Negative). Companies that participate now secure an advantageous position as environmental leaders.

standard.title: ESG reporting now has to prove 'action.'
standard.lead: Investors, consumers, and regulators now demand answers to the following questions, not declarations.

questions.text: What specifically did you do last year?
questions.desc: Evidence of action — not declarations or plans.

questions.text: How much did your environmental metrics improve?
questions.desc: Quantitative figures — kg, count, time, coordinates.

questions.text: How can you prove this objectively?
questions.desc: Third-party verification — international NGOs and standards mapping.

standard.warn: If you cannot answer clearly, you face accusations of greenwashing. Both the EU CSRD and ISSB specify verifiable data as a core requirement.

cycle.title: A simple but powerful 4-step cycle
cycle.lead: Repeated every quarter, this cycle produces the quantitative results in your ESG report.

steps.title: Education (Certification)
steps.desc: Support for earning PADI scuba / freediver international certifications. Certified members take the additional Dive Against Debris® Specialty course.

steps.title: Underwater cleanup
steps.desc: Teams of 2–3 conduct buddy dives to collect ghost nets, plastic, metal, glass, and more. Accompanied by professional guides and operated within a safe depth range of 2–10m.

steps.title: Data upload
steps.desc: Item, weight, GPS, and timestamp data are registered in the Dive Against Debris® global database. Used as policy material by international organizations.

steps.title: ESG reporting
steps.desc: Quarterly summaries → a year-end integrated report. Automatically mapped to GRI 306 · ISO 14001 · SDG 14. Immediately reflected in your sustainability report.

cycle.freq: Four times a year, repeated every quarter — a sustainable process, not a one-off event.

overview.title: Project Overview
overview.description: Introduction to MOBA's phased business plan and strategy.
overview.detailedDescription: The MOBA project achieves its goals of marine environment protection through a systematic 4-phase approach. Each phase builds upon the achievements of the previous phase, and our ultimate goal is to create a sustainable marine protection ecosystem.

phases.title: Execution Process
phases.subtitle: Education (Certification) → Ploving (Underwater Cleanup) → Data Upload → ESG Reporting

phase1.title: Phase 1: Education & Certification
activities: Dive Against Debris® training (collection, safety, data)
Safety equipment and collection tools provision

phase2.title: Phase 2: Underwater Cleanup (Ploving)
activities: Removal of ghost nets and plastics
Precise GPS, item, weight, count, photo logging

phase3.title: Phase 3: Data Upload & Processing
phase3.description: Upload to international DB and legal waste processing
activities: Upload to Dive Against Debris® platform
Use for UNEP and policy development

phase4.title: Phase 4: ESG Reporting
activities: Environment: volumes, item ratios, carbon reduction
Social: participants, volunteer hours, local cooperation
Governance: safety training, insurance, third-party verification

phase5.title: Phase 5: Visualization Project
phase5.description: Transform collection outcomes into local cultural assets
activities: Create murals, sculptures, and boat paintings using collected debris
Co-create with local artists, youth, and fishers
Display cleanup data on-site via signage and QR codes
Preserve as permanent local cultural assets
